summary:
ARES (Advanced Rover & Explorer System) is a Mars exploration and mission-planning platform focused on Gale Crater and Curiosity’s traverse toward Mount Sharp. It combines planetary datasets and geospatial tools to help users examine terrain, identify potential hazards, explore scientific observations, and plan rover routes.

ARES integrates NASA/PDS data, including MGS MOLA elevation models (~463 m/pixel), two MRO HiRISE stereo Digital Terrain Models (~1.01 m/pixel), Curiosity traverse records, archived MSL RAD radiation measurements, and historical REMS atmospheric observations. A live NASA Mars Trek CTX basemap provides visual context. Features include interactive mapping, terrain analysis, slope and Terrain Ruggedness Index (TRI) calculations, hazard assessment, science locations, environmental visualizations, data provenance, and A* pathfinding.

ARES distinguishes measured data, derived results, engineering estimates, and unavailable data. It accounts for differences in resolution and treats areas without high-resolution coverage as unknown rather than safe. RAD and REMS records are historical, not live feeds, and THEMIS thermal-inertia data is not yet integrated.

ARES is an experimental decision-support demonstrator. Its terrain assessments and routes are preliminary aids, not NASA-certified safety recommendations. Its goal is to make Mars data accessible and show how planetary science, geospatial analysis, and computational planning can support robotic exploration.
details:
ARES — Advanced Rover & Explorer System

Project Overview

ARES (Advanced Rover & Explorer System) is a web-based prototype designed to bring together different aspects of Mars surface exploration in one integrated platform.

Exploring Mars involves understanding its terrain, environmental conditions, potential hazards, and scientifically interesting locations. ARES aims to make these different layers of information easier to explore through a unified interface.

Key Features

  • Mars Exploration Map: An interactive map for exploring Martian locations, including areas around Gale Crater.
  • Terrain Analysis: Tools for examining terrain characteristics and understanding surface conditions.
  • Hazard Awareness: A system for classifying potential surface hazards.
  • Environmental Intelligence: An interface for exploring environmental information relevant to Mars missions.
  • Rover Route Planning: A route-planning prototype that demonstrates how a rover might navigate across a selected terrain.
  • Scientific Exploration: A dedicated section for exploring scientific information and points of interest.

Our Goal

Our goal is to demonstrate how an integrated digital exploration platform could help future Mars explorers understand their surroundings, examine relevant scientific information, and investigate possible rover routes.

Technologies

The project uses React, TypeScript, Vite, OpenLayers, and Recharts, alongside other supporting libraries.
